verdict.rationale: Codegen operates autonomously by default (creating PRs, committing code, running tasks without per-step human confirmation) and exposes 'agent-behavior' and 'agent-permissions' settings pages, implying some configurability of oversight, but the evidence never documents an explicit 'auto-approve all actions' toggle versus a step-by-step confirmation mode — instead it shows agents presenting a structured plan per step, which suggests some interactive checkpointing exists. Missing for 10: an explicit setting/flag to disable per-action confirmation, documentation contrasting confirm-each-step vs auto-approve modes, and independent confirmation of this behavior.
